structure: A single 30-line Markdown ruling file (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-10-07.md) from Sam, dated 7 October 2026. Lines 3-21 are the verbatim quote in five paragraphs: the goal, the DR1 parity backlog's role (with one elision marked [...]), precedence, decisions (questions kept to a minimum) and themes. Lines 23-30 are the main session's reading of it as 8 numbered claims, each marked New (none answers an earlier report question). Scope is the whole file; nothing is left out. It is one part.

parts.title: Whole ruling
parts.scope: The whole file: the verbatim quote (lines 3-21) and the 8 numbered claims (lines 23-30). There is no other part.
covers: The 5 quoted paragraphs: goal, DR1 parity backlog role, precedence, decisions on questions for people, themes

The 8 numbered claims, each checked against the quote and recorded verbatim or inferred: (1) real services change to match DR2.1; (2) repos that change are worked out from evidence; (3) DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements; (4) DR1 used only where the real frontend and prototype clash, judgement followed and row cited; (5) prototype wins by default; (6) only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint (persistence, validation, authentication, cross-service behaviour) overrides it; (7) questions for people kept to a minimum, raised only when truly exceptional and unsettled by default or DR1; (8) increments grouped into themes bounded by the code they touch, buildable in parallel without conflicting PRs
Any gap the ruling leaves open on what it touches, such as the [...] elision in the DR1 paragraph or what counts as 'truly exceptional', recorded as gap claims
